name: multi-tenant-saas
description: Workspaces of different teams share one deployment. The output must set tenancy to multi and carry a mandatory tenant-isolation requirement whose criteria prove cross-workspace access is denied.

configuration.name: Pulse Analytics
configuration.description: SaaS analytics dashboard for small teams with workspaces, subscription billing, and a companion mobile app for alerts.

requirements.custom: Workspace owners can invite members with viewer or editor roles.

context.goal: An analytics dashboard where small teams track their metrics in shared workspaces and receive mobile alerts.
context.scope: Web dashboard, workspaces with roles, subscription billing, admin dashboard, and a mobile app for alerts.

personas.name: Workspace owner
personas.description: Creates a workspace, pays for it, and invites members.

personas.name: Member
personas.description: Views (viewer) or edits (editor) a workspace's dashboards.

operations.statement: Users can sign up, sign in, and belong to one or more workspaces.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can register, sign in, and see the workspaces they belong to.

operations.statement: Workspace owners can invite members as viewers or editors; viewers cannot change anything.
acceptance_criteria: An invited viewer can open dashboards but every edit request is rejected.

operations.statement: Each workspace has a paid subscription managed by its owner.
acceptance_criteria: A test subscription activates a workspace, and cancelling it is reflected in the workspace.

operations.statement: Each workspace's data is visible and changeable only by that workspace's members.
acceptance_criteria: A member of workspace A receives 404 for any dashboard, alert, or record of workspace B.
Automated tests attempt cross-workspace reads and writes and verify they are denied.

operations.statement: Members receive metric alerts as push notifications in the mobile app.
acceptance_criteria: A triggered alert reaches a signed-in member's phone within one minute.

operations.statement: Core flows are covered by automated tests that run on every change.
acceptance_criteria: CI runs unit, integration, and end-to-end tests and blocks merging on failure.

questions.prompt: Where does the analytics data come from?
questions.why: Data sources decide the integrations, storage, and cost.
options: Our own product's events via an API
Third-party tools such as Stripe or Google Analytics

questions.why: Pricing tiers decide plan limits and billing logic.

decisions: Workspaces of different teams share one deployment, so tenant isolation is a must-have.
